newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin meets PM, set to host Spanish king.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin meets PM, set to host Spanish king.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, who has been resting at his country residence, began a busy work schedule on Monday by meeting his Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, a Kremlin spokesman said.

He did not say what the two men discussed but Interfax news agency said their talks focused on Russia's economic and social problems and the issue of national security following a rash of violent attacks apparently linked to breakaway Chechnya.
Interfax said reforming Russia's natural monopolies -- gas, electricity and telecommunications -- and tackling the intractable problem of wage arrears would feature in their discussions.
Earlier this year Yeltsin drafted young liberals into the government in a bid to drag Russia out of its economic depression and revive flagging market reforms.
Yeltsin was also expected on Monday to meet Ivan Rybkin, secretary of the Security Council, the spokesman said.

Interfax said Rybkin would brief the president on his recent peace talks with Chechnya's separatist leadership. Russia and Chechnya are trying to forge a comprehensive accord mapping out relations after 21 months of war which ended last August.
Russia has beefed up security in recent days after two bomb explosions in southern Russia killed four people. Radical Chechen commander Salman Raduyev has claimed responsibility for the attacks.
Later on Monday Yeltsin will attend a welcoming ceremony in the Kremlin for King Juan Carlos of Spain, who is coming to Russia for a three-day state visit.
